| [THEORY-365](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-365.md) v4 | HNSW cost grew logarithmically in uniform tests | Malkov and Yashunin (2020), [LIT-1098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1098.md), read in [NOTE-916](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-916.md) from arXiv v4. They build an index like a skip list, with proximity graphs in place of linked lists, and argue that search costs a constant per layer over O(log N) layers. That holds if each layer is an exact Delaunay graph of bounded mean degree. HNSW does not build such graphs, and Delaunay degree grows exponentially with dimension. For the graphs it does build, cost no worse than logarithmic is measured on uniform random data at d = 8, a saturating beam width at d = 4, and at d = 128 (200M SIFT) the growth departs from a logarithm. A proof for the graphs HNSW builds is QUESTION-187. The paper gives no worst-case bound and no recall guarantee. Construction is argued to cost about N searches. | Active |
| [THEORY-370](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-370.md) | Small-world search is fast only at r = 2 | Kleinberg (2000), [LIT-1103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1103.md), read in [NOTE-923](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-923.md). Proved for the two-dimensional lattice: with nodes, local links and the number of long-range links fixed, changing only the exponent r of the long-range link distribution moves the expected delivery time of the best decentralized searcher from O((log n)²) at r = 2 to a power of n at every other r, including r = 0, where paths of polylogarithmic length exist. The upper bound is proved only for one local and one long-range link per node; the k-dimensional statement (r = k) is asserted, not proved; the family is inverse power laws of a distance every node can compute, so it does not show that no other link structure is navigable. | Active |
| [THEORY-385](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-385.md) v3 | HNSW heuristic links keep clustered data reachable | Malkov and Yashunin (2020), [LIT-1098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1098.md), read in [NOTE-916](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-916.md). In HNSW, each new element's neighbours are chosen either as its M nearest candidates or by a pruning rule that keeps a candidate only if it is nearer the new element than to any neighbour already kept, a rule related to the relative neighbourhood graph. On 10M random d = 10 vectors in 100 isolated clusters, nearest-neighbour links failed to reach high recall and the pruning rule did not. In every test reported, the rule was at least as good. Its gain was largest at low dimension, at high recall, and on clustered data, and small on uniform or very high-dimensional data. These are the authors' benchmarks: one clustered dataset, synthetic, with no independent replication in this reading. Re-run independently at smaller scale on promotion (2026-10-20), with the same result. | Active |
| [THEORY-421](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-421.md) v3 | Hyperbolic radius only partly reads hierarchy | Yang, Zhou, Ying, Chen & King (2023), [LIT-871](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md), read in [NOTE-669](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-669.md). On two synthetic 3-ary trees of eight levels, HGCN leaves the root at hyperbolic distance 1.8–3.3 from the origin where the minimum is 1.2–2.4, the distances are roughly normal rather than leaf-heavy, and radius orders true levels for 69–75% of 5,000 random pairs. Recentring on the centroid plus an outward push raises that to 75–84%. The diagnosis rests on one architecture, two synthetic trees and one table without variance, and the paper does not separate a real failure to order levels from the origin's arbitrariness under losses that see only pairwise distances. | Active |
| [THEORY-422](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-422.md) v2 | No network is best for every group-learning task | Zollman (2013), [LIT-716](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-716.md), a survey read in [NOTE-567](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-567.md). | [THEORY-456](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-456.md) | Ricci flow separates communities, but weakly | Ni, Lin, Luo & Gao (2019), [LIT-004](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-004.md), read in full with its SI in [NOTE-006](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-006.md), which checked Lemma E.1 by linear programming and iterated the proof's matrix. Repeated averaging with fixed weights is a Markov chain run on opinions, and whether it ends in agreement is a question about the chain's closed classes and their periods. It is not about how much each member trusts itself. The weights are fixed and no evidence enters, so nothing here says the consensus is right, and the periodic failure is a discrete-time one. | Active |
| [THEORY-993](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-993.md) v2 | MMSB memberships are unidentified up to R | Airoldi, Blei, Fienberg and Xing (2008), [LIT-1553](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1553.md), read in [NOTE-1179](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1179.md). The paper says the blockmodel and the memberships do not compete, because one is global and asymmetric and the other local and symmetric. Given the memberships they do: a change of block basis moves every node's memberships toward the centre and sharpens B, with the same edge probabilities. What can still separate them is the Dirichlet family assumed for memberships, not the graph. The confounding of ρ with B's scale is exact even in the marginal likelihood. | Active |
| [THEORY-1008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1008.md) | MMSB memberships predict protein function | Airoldi, Blei, Fienberg and Xing (2008), [LIT-1553](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1553.md), §4.3.2 and Figs. 10–12, read in [NOTE-1179](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1179.md). The batch's one check of inferred mixed memberships against labels the model never saw. The reported margin is over a weak baseline, so it shows less than it seems: probably some information, not yet how much. It says nothing about whether the fifteen blocks are the fifteen functions. | Proposed |

Proposed for both steps. It does not say that recovery is cheap on every graph, under every noise model, or for fine angular resolution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1059.md) v2 | Synchrony restricts to quotient network dynamics | Stewart, Golubitsky and Pivato (2003), [LIT-1674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1674.md), read in [NOTE-1217](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1217.md): the quotient construction (§7), Theorems 8.3, 8.4 and 9.2 with proofs, the counterexample of Remark 7.5 and Example 7.1. Active as mathematics. The quotient describes the dynamics on the invariant subspace exactly, but only a subclass of the quotient's own admissible dynamics arises that way, and nothing is said about stability transverse to the subspace. | Active |

Active as mathematics: the convergence is a theorem about a linear heat equation, and the gap between expressed and held opinion is in the definitions and is worked in an example. | [THEORY-1129](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1129.md) | Fused GW anchors break ties only if they move | Derived from Vayer et al. In toy circuits inspired by C. elegans, a sigmoidal edge gates transmission, and moderate drive turns a connection into a fractional-derivative-like kernel, while saturation removes the effect. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2005](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2005.md) | Graph fibrations induce maps of network dynamics | From the reading of [LIT-2792](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2792.md) in [NOTE-2130](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2130.md). DeVille and Lerman (2013), arXiv 1303.3907. In a coordinate-free framework of networks of control systems on manifolds, they prove that a graph fibration (Boldi and Vigna's unique lifting of incoming edges, equivalently input-tree isomorphism) induces a map of dynamical systems in the opposite direction for every modular vector field. Surjective fibrations, which include quotients by balanced relations, embed the quotient's dynamics as an invariant synchrony polydiagonal. Injective fibrations project a network onto the subsystem that drives it, which they call an abstraction. Only this direction is proved, and stability is not treated. Here because it is the fibration form of the balanced-partition result held as [THEORY-1065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1065.md) and [THEORY-1059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1059.md), which it generalizes in one direction. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |

A mixed-integer program deletes the fewest tracts from a baseline connectome (five fibres, each an orbit) until each state's observed synchrony clusters are its coarsest balanced colouring. Rest gives four fibres, both tasks five, all with only the identity automorphism, and the rest and task partitions are not ordered by refinement. The account applies [THEORY-1065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1065.md): synchrony classes without symmetry. It goes past that theorem in calling an invariant partition "proven to be synchronous", and it predicts no partition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2054](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2054.md) | Bipartite SBM recovers groups projections hide | From the reading of [LIT-2809](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2809.md) in [NOTE-2095](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2095.md). Larremore, Clauset and Jacobs (2014), arXiv 1403.2933. They formulate a degree-corrected bipartite stochastic block model, in which communities are pure-type groups with the same expected connection pattern to the other side's groups. It finds better partitions faster than the unconstrained SBM and recovers planted structure that one-mode projections hide. In their actor–movie example (IMDb, 1995–2000), five of six movie blocks were language groups and one was a genre (Adult), and the authors read the blocks as traces of "multiple mechanisms responsible for the existence of edges". Here because it is the standard method behind the owner's U10 genres example, [CASE-296](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-296.md): it supplies the joint people-and-items identification, but its own film blocks are mostly not genres, which bears on the case's confounds. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2055.md) | Covering partitions only coarsen under GD | From the reading of [LIT-2843](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2843.md) in [NOTE-2085](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2085.md). Velarde, Parra, Hashemi and Makse (2026), arXiv 2609.01768 (v1, not peer reviewed). They carry graph fibrations to weighted layered networks as balanced colourings of units. They prove that a covering partition (equal colour- summed input and output weights) can only coarsen under gradient descent, and report that tolerance-defined quasi-covers grow during training of an MLP, a CNN and an LSTM agent, allowing compression to 17–18% of size; transformers are shown compressed, not tracked in training. Fibers here are computed with every input coordinate its own colour, so they are input-independent redundancies, not quotients of inputs, and the paper has no relational or rule task. Here because it is the evidence on the fibration side of the owner's U9 hunch, QUESTION- tmpex36a: it shows that balanced structure among units is learned without symmetry forcing it, and is silent on role abstraction. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |

The owner's own method, named at U37 as a place to see communities forming subcommunities. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
